tables.purpose: This table records individual product return transactions. It tracks which order and order line item is being returned, the return date, reason, processing status, and the refund amount.

column_meanings.meaning: Unique identifier for the return record.
Identifier of the original order linked to this return.
Identifier of the specific order line item that is being returned.
Date and time when the return was recorded.
Text code describing why the product was returned (e.g., changed_mind, wrong_item, defective).
Current processing state of the return (e.g., approved, refunded, pending).
Monetary amount paid back to the customer for the return.

tables.relationships: order_id links to orders.order_id and order_item_id links to order_items.order_item_id.
tables.business_value: Enables analysis of return reasons, volumes, and financial impact of refunds, as well as linking returns back to original orders for customer service follow‑up.

ambiguity_flags.note: Currency is not indicated in the sample; amount is likely monetary but the unit (e.g., USD) is unclear.

Status records return processing state; other tables also have a status column with different value sets, only the word 'refunded' overlaps, which may be coincidental rather than a defined relationship.

tables.purpose: This table stores information about product suppliers. It tracks each supplier's name, country of operation, contact email, and current status.

column_meanings.meaning: Unique identifier for the supplier.
Legal or commercial name of the supplier.
Country where the supplier is based.
Email address for contacting the supplier.
Current activity state of the supplier (sample shows 'active').

tables.business_value: Supports reporting on supplier geography, activity status, and enables joins to product data to analyse supplier performance.

ambiguity_flags.note: Status indicates supplier activity, but other tables use a status column for different concepts; overlap is limited to generic words like 'active'.
Country lists supplier locations; customers also have a country column for customer residence with different values, and no overlapping values are seen in the samples.

tables.purpose: This table keeps a snapshot of stock levels for each product. It records how many units are on hand, the reorder threshold, and when the record was last updated.

column_meanings.meaning: Unique identifier for the inventory record.
Identifier of the product to which the stock counts belong.
Number of units currently available in inventory.
Minimum quantity that triggers a reorder request.
Timestamp of the most recent inventory count update.

tables.business_value: Allows calculation of stock availability, identification of items needing replenishment, and timing of inventory updates.

tables.purpose: This table logs marketing campaigns run by the company. It tracks each campaign's name, channel, dates, budget, and lifecycle status.

column_meanings.meaning: Unique identifier for the campaign.
Descriptive name of the marketing effort.
Medium used for the campaign (e.g., social_media, affiliate, paid_search).
Date when the campaign began.
Date when the campaign ended or null if ongoing.
Planned monetary spend for the campaign.
Current lifecycle stage of the campaign (active, completed, paused).

tables.business_value: Enables evaluation of marketing spend effectiveness, channel performance, and campaign timing.

ambiguity_flags.note: Channel refers to marketing medium; orders also have a channel column for sales channels (in_store, marketplace, etc.) with different values and no overlap.
Status indicates campaign lifecycle; other tables use status for unrelated concepts, with only generic words overlapping, so the meaning is likely distinct.

tables.purpose: This table contains records for each customer. It tracks personal contact details, signup date, country of residence, segment classification, and current activity status.

column_meanings.meaning: Unique identifier for the customer.
Customer's email address.
Customer's given name.
Customer's family name.
Date the customer account was created.
Country where the customer resides.
Business-assigned group indicating customer value or risk (e.g., new, at_risk, high_value, regular).
Current activity state of the customer account (active, inactive, churned).

tables.business_value: Supports segmentation analysis, churn prediction, and geographic distribution of the customer base.

ambiguity_flags.note: Status reflects customer activity; other tables have a status column for different entities, with only generic overlap, suggesting distinct meanings.
Country lists customer residency; suppliers also have a country column for supplier location with different values and no overlap in the samples.

tables.purpose: This table records each purchase order placed by a customer. It tracks the customer, order date, sales channel, current order status, and total monetary amount.

column_meanings.meaning: Unique identifier for the order.
Identifier of the customer who placed the order.
Timestamp when the order was created.
Current fulfillment or financial state of the order (e.g., cancelled, refunded, delivered).
Sales channel through which the order was made (in_store, marketplace, mobile_app, web).
Total monetary value of the order.

tables.business_value: Enables revenue reporting, channel performance analysis, and monitoring of order lifecycle stages.

ambiguity_flags.note: Monetary unit is not specified; assumed to be a currency but the exact type (e.g., USD) is unclear.
Status records order fulfillment state; other tables also have a status column with different vocabularies, only generic overlap observed.
Channel indicates sales channel; marketing_campaigns also has a channel column for marketing mediums with different values and no overlap.

tables.purpose: This table lists the individual line items that belong to each order. It records which product was sold, the quantity, and the price per unit at the time of sale.

column_meanings.meaning: Unique identifier for the order line item.
Identifier of the order that contains this line item.
Identifier of the product being sold.
Number of units of the product purchased in this line item.
Price per single unit of the product for this line item.

tables.relationships: order_id links to orders.order_id and product_id links to products.product_id.
tables.business_value: Supports detailed revenue breakdowns, product popularity tracking, and calculation of average selling price per product.

ambiguity_flags.note: Currency for the unit price is not indicated in the sample data.

tables.purpose: This table catalogs the products that can be sold. It tracks each product's name, category, price, availability status, and its supplier.

column_meanings.meaning: Unique identifier for the product.
Descriptive name of the product.
Business category or segment the product belongs to (e.g., beauty, toys, home_goods, sports).
Standard selling price for the product.
Current availability state of the product (active, discontinued, out_of_stock).
Identifier of the supplier that provides this product.

tables.business_value: Allows analysis of product pricing, category performance, and supplier contributions to the catalog.

ambiguity_flags.note: Monetary unit is not specified; assumed to be a currency but the exact type is unclear.
Status indicates product availability; other tables also have a status column with differing vocabularies, only generic overlap, suggesting separate meanings.
